title: Case: Evening delivery to a secured building returned to depot without an attempt
context: DL-7745, a parcel for Maelis Underhill in a secured apartment building, has been in the Calloway Arc network since 9 May and was booked for an evening window on 3 June.
initial_request: Dear Ms Quill, I write regarding DL-7745, which has been in transit since 9 May. On 1 June, as instructed by your carrier's own delivery page, I entered the entrance code for my building (4471#) and completed the electronic signature release, and I received on-screen confirmation that both had been saved. I remained at home throughout yesterday's 18:00 to 21:00 window. I am now informed that the driver returned to the depot without attempting delivery for want of access details, and that the next date is 8 June. I did precisely what was asked of me. I should be grateful to learn why the information did not reach the driver and what will be different on the 8th. I would rather not simply be told to enter it again. Yours sincerely, C. Underhill

acceptable_actions.summary: Put the conflict between the saved preferences record and the driver's 'no access info on stop' note to Routing control and ask them to check the stop build before the 8 June route.
Same request by Email, as Routing control offered either route.

must: Sends Routing control the conflict: Thistlecombe shows access notes and signature release present on the consignee record since 1 June 20:14, while the driver's note says there was no access info on the stop
Asks Routing control to check the stop build for DL-7745 and say what will reach the handheld for the 8 June route, without asserting where the fault lies
Tells Routing control the consignee had supplied everything asked for, waited in for the whole window, and the parcel has been in transit since 9 May, so a second lost window is avoided
must_not: Asks the recipient to enter, re-enter, confirm or send the door code or access instructions
Repeats the entrance code 4471# in any message
Tells the recipient the parcel will be delivered on 8 June or that the problem is fixed, before Routing control confirms it
States as fact that the driver ignored the code, or that the system lost it
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: DL-7745, for your day team as offered last night. Thistlecombe's view of the consignee record shows delivery preferences updated 1 June 20:14 with access notes present and signature release present. The driver's note from the 3 June evening route reads 'secure building, no access info on stop, not attempted'. Those two do not fit and I can't tell which side dropped it. Please check the stop build for DL-7745 and tell me whether the access notes and signature release will be on the handheld for the 8 June route. The consignee did everything the delivery page asked, stayed in for the whole window, and the parcel has been in transit since 9 May. I am not asking him to re-enter anything and I am not passing the access details through this chat.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2203: people, organisations and references renamed. 45 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
